title: Forced Index Membership Events
purpose: Define the minimum auditable event dataset needed before testing index-addition, deletion, or reconstitution pressure without leaking future information.
data_grain: event calendar plus daily OHLCV, volume, and liquidity proxies
candidate_sources: index provider methodology and rebalance announcement archives
ETF or index fund holdings snapshots when official historical constituent files are unavailable
exchange or issuer press releases for additions, deletions, and corporate-action-driven index changes
survivorship-aware historical price and volume data for every affected symbol
quoted spread, high-low spread proxy, or conservative bps cost proxy
construction_rules: Use announcement_date for tradability and information timing; effective_date alone is not enough.
Keep additions and deletions as separate event_type values before any return analysis.
Preserve source notes per event row; do not merge events from undocumented secondary lists without provenance.
Require price, volume, and liquidity coverage before and after each event window.
Do not add or remove event types after inspecting event returns.
Keep delisted or acquired symbols in the event universe when they were tradable at announcement time.
quality_checks: announcement_date must be on or before effective_date for every event.
announcement_date and effective_date must map to valid trading sessions or include an explicit non-trading-day adjustment rule.
Every row must include source_name and source_url_or_note.
At least one pre-event liquidity estimate must exist for every tested symbol.
Events missing survivorship-safe post-event prices must be labeled and excluded only by a prespecified rule.
minimum_viable_tests: No-trade event study by event_type around announcement and effective windows.
Separate addition and deletion cohorts before any combined strategy result.
Liquidity-bucket summary showing whether the effect is concentrated where personal-capital capacity is plausible.
Cost sensitivity using conservative spread or bps assumptions before any executable strategy.
A single fixed holding-period test only after the no-trade diagnostics identify a plausible direction.
known_limitations: Official historical constituent and announcement archives may be paid, incomplete, or hard to normalize.
ETF holdings snapshots are an imperfect proxy for index membership and can introduce timing ambiguity.
Daily data may miss close auction, rebalance-on-close, and intraday liquidity effects.
Index methodology changes can make older and newer events less comparable.
The current backtester does not yet model market impact, borrow, or close-auction execution.
next_action: Find one auditable free or exported source for historical index additions/deletions with announcement and effective dates before creating any executable forced-flow strategy.
